standard.title: Elements of dance communicate meaning
standard.description: explore ways that the elements of dance are combined to communicate ideas, perspectives and/or meaning in dance across cultures, times, places and/or other contexts
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can explore where, why and how dance is choreographed and/or performed across cultures, times, places and/or other contexts (Y3-4). They can compare dances and identify purpose and meaning using Viewpoints questions.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students explore ways that the elements of dance are combined to communicate ideas, perspectives and/or meaning in dance across cultures, times, places and/or other contexts.

nodes.label: Reading element use in observed dances
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify and describe how elements of dance and choreographic devices are combined in dances they experience — connecting element choices to communicative effect.
nodes.minimum_width: Identifying how at least two elements of dance are used together in one observed dance — and describing the communicative effect of those choices.
nodes.typical_width: Exploring how dances use elements and choreographic devices (repetition, unison, contrast); discussing purpose of movements, elements, production elements, technical and expressive skills and their effect on mood and audience relationship; using Viewpoints to explore similarities and differences across choreographers and contexts.
wider: Explore how dance communicates cultural traditions — examining a dance from a country or region in Asia and asking how it reflects cultural ways of being
Investigate how elements of dance in a specific dance style (e.g. hip hop, contemporary, classical) reflect the cultural or historical context of that style
nodes.hinge_reason: Reading element combinations as communicative — not just aesthetic — is the analytical move that distinguishes appreciation from analysis. Students who cannot yet do this will engage with dances at a descriptive surface level in Y7-8 investigating work.

response_modes.reason: Element-to-meaning reading requires an explicit interpretive move — students need Viewpoints questions with analytical scaffolding: 'How does the use of slow dynamics here change the mood?', 'What does the unison say about the relationship between dancers?'

success_criteria: Student can describe how at least two elements combine in an observed dance to create a specific communicative effect
Student connects at least one element choice to the mood, meaning or audience relationship in the dance

nodes.label: Comparing element use across cultural contexts
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can compare how elements of dance are combined across different cultural and temporal contexts — identifying how context shapes element use.
nodes.minimum_width: Comparing element use in two dances from different cultural or temporal contexts — identifying at least one difference in how elements are combined and suggesting why.
nodes.typical_width: Exploring similarities and differences in how choreographers use elements across genres, styles, cultures and times; using Viewpoints to develop questions about how main ideas are communicated; seeking feedback about how audience perceived choreographic intent; considering how cultural traditions shape element use.
wider: Investigate how dance-on-screen (film, music video) uses production elements alongside dance elements — examining how the combination changes what is communicated
Explore how a dance from a country or region in Asia uses elements in ways that differ from familiar Western dance styles — discussing what this reveals about cultural values and aesthetics

response_modes.reason: Genuine comparison requires genuine diversity of examples. Students who have encountered only one or two cultural dance contexts cannot make meaningful comparative observations.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Students who compare element use across genuinely diverse cultural contexts develop the cultural-analytical literacy that underpins the sophisticated investigating work of Y7-8 and Y9-10.
success_criteria: Student can compare element use in two dances from different cultural or temporal contexts
Student offers a culturally contextualised explanation for at least one difference observed
